review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped uses of orb, oi, orho, ordOrbit_mk and ord_smul_eq under LeanModularForms/ValenceFormula. I read the TextbookExistence orbit lemmas. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested. The existing @[simp] ordOrbit_mk is fine: it is a rfl lemma, its LHS is bigger than its RHS, and it can't loop. The gaps are that the orbit map `orb` has no simp lemma for how it interacts with the group action, and that the order-invariance lemma is not tagged simp.

findings.declaration: orb (missing simp lemma `orb (g • p) = orb p`)
findings.excerpt: def orb (p : ℍ) : Orbit := Quotient.mk'' p
findings.problem: `orb` is an opaque def with only one simp lemma, `ordOrbit_mk`. There is no canonical simp lemma saying `orb (g • p) = orb p` for `g : SL(2, ℤ)`. There is also no iff lemma `orb p = orb q ↔ ∃ g, g • p = q`. As a result, downstream files re-prove the special cases by hand. Each proof starts with `change Quotient.mk'' … = Quotient.mk'' …`, which unfolds `orb` and breaks the abstraction. Examples are `orb_vAdd_neg_one_eq` and `orb_S_smul_eq` in TextbookExistence. `orb_rho_plus_one_eq_orb_rho` in this file does the same. Expressions like `orb (S • p)` or `orb (T • p)` therefore do not normalize to `orb p` under `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Right after `orb`, add `@[simp] theorem orb_smul (g : SL(2, ℤ)) (p : ℍ) : orb (g • p) = orb p := Quotient.sound' ⟨g, rfl⟩`. This is the same step already used inline in `orbit_has_fd_rep`. The orientation is safe: the LHS is larger and the RHS is a subterm, so it cannot loop. Add an `orb_eq_orb_iff` lemma stating `orb p = orb q ↔ ∃ g : SL(2, ℤ), g • q = p`, with the direction and form to be checked against `Quotient.exact'`. Use `orb_smul` to shorten `orb_S_smul_eq` and `orb_vAdd_neg_one_eq`, and use the iff lemma in place of the repeated `Quotient.eq''`/`orbitRel_apply`/`mem_orbit_iff` rewrites.
findings.benefit: Orbit equalities involving `S •` and `T •`, and any other SL(2,ℤ) translate, close by `simp`. The `Quotient.mk''` implementation detail stays inside this file instead of leaking into `change` steps in TextbookExistence and TextbookForm.

evidence.excerpt: change Quotient.mk'' ((-1 : ℝ) +ᵥ p) = Quotient.mk'' p

findings.excerpt:
theorem ord_smul_eq (g : SL(2, ℤ)) (p : ℍ) :
    orderOfVanishingAt' (⇑f) (g • p) = orderOfVanishingAt' (⇑f) p
findings.problem: `ord_smul_eq` is the main invariance statement, but it is not a simp lemma. The related `ordOrbit_mk` is `@[simp]`. Together with the missing `orb_smul`, a goal such as `orderOfVanishingAt' f (g • p) = …` or `ordOrbit f (orb (g • p)) = …` cannot be simplified fully. The orientation is already canonical: the LHS is `g • p` and the RHS is the stripped term. `f` is explicit and appears on both sides, `g` and `p` are bound variables, and there are no hypotheses, so the lemma is a good simp candidate.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the theorem `@[simp]`. Together with `orb_smul`, this lets simp reduce `orderOfVanishingAt' f (g • p)` to `orderOfVanishingAt' f p`. Note that `ord_S_eq` and `ord_add_one_eq`, used in the proof, are specific cases that the general lemma subsumes after the generator induction.
findings.benefit: Later orbit-sum arguments can discharge invariance side goals by `simp` instead of spelling out `rw [← ordOrbit_mk …]` plus an explicit `ord_smul_eq f g p`. The simp set then handles `g • p` consistently at both the point level (`ord_smul_eq`) and the orbit level (`ordOrbit_mk` plus `orb_smul`).

evidence.excerpt: theorem ordOrbit_mk (p : ℍ) : ordOrbit f (orb p) = orderOfVanishingAt' (⇑f) p := rfl
